_comment: Detection rules quoted in the report: YARA (one compiles, one does not), Suricata, Snort, Sigma, auto-linked to MidnightFrost by title.
report_text:
MidnightFrost detection notes

The following YARA rule detects the MidnightFrost loader in memory:

rule MidnightFrost_Loader {
    meta:
        description = "MidnightFrost loader strings"
    strings:
        $a = "FrostSvc" ascii
        $b = "MidnightFrostMtx" wide
    condition:
        any of them
}

A second rule is broken in the report (its condition names a string that does not exist):

rule Broken_Rule {
    strings:
        $a = "oops"
    condition:
        $nonexistent
}

The network side is covered by this Suricata rule:

alert http $HOME_NET any -> $EXTERNAL_NET any (msg:"MidnightFrost beacon"; content:"/stage/payload.bin"; http.uri; sid:1000001; rev:1;)

Snort users can use the older rule below.
alert tcp $HOME_NET any -> $EXTERNAL_NET 4444 (msg:"MidnightFrost reverse shell"; flow:to_server,established; content:"|de ad be ef|"; sid:1000002; rev:1;)

The host indicators are 91.215.85.17, frostmail-cdn.test and the hash e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855.

Sigma rule for the registry persistence:

title: MidnightFrost Run Key Persistence
id: 5f1c1d52-3c2b-4a58-9d1f-0b8f9a3c7e11
status: experimental
description: Detects the FrostSvc Run key written by MidnightFrost
logsource:
    category: registry_set
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|endswith: '\CurrentVersion\Run\FrostSvc'
    condition: selection
level: high
